hook: Rule four: don’t answer the phone.
excerpt: At the foot of the stairs, on a walnut console, was a telephone.

excerpt.text: He walked me back into the hallway and tapped the base of the cream telephone with one finger. ‘Rule four. Don’t answer this.’

excerpt: At ten to two I gave up, put on the robe and went down for a glass of water.

excerpt.text: I didn’t turn the lights on. I don’t know why.
At seven minutes past two it rang.

excerpt: It wasn’t loud. It was a soft, polite electronic trill, the sound of something designed not to frighten anyone, and in that silence it went through me like a dropped tray.

excerpt.text: I stood there with the glass in my hand and counted. Four. Five. Six. On the eighth ring it stopped.
A person, with a phone in their hand, at two in the morning, ringing a house where nobody was supposed to answer.

caption:
Rule four: don’t answer the phone.

Ava is house-sitting on a remote Cornish headland. Three weeks, generous pay, a few simple rules.

Then, at two o’clock one morning, the old cream telephone at the foot of the stairs begins to ring.
